violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw shelled eggs stored above box of uncooked RTE broccoli inside the Amerikooler walk in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. CDI: CFM relocated the box of uncooked broccoli to the top shelf inside the Amerikooler walk in refrigerator.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: plastic containers of raw bean sprouts, cooked noodles, cut cabbage stored on prep counter out of temperature control (not on TPHC) across for the wok station on the cookline.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CDI: CFM relocated the plastic containers of raw bean sprouts, cooked noodles, cut cabbage to the inside of the Amerikooler walk in refrigerator to cool to 41F or below. CFM agreed to stored the plastic containers of raw bean sprouts, cooked noodles, cut cabbage inside the Dukers 2 Dr preptop refrigerator (left unit across from wok station on cookline) stored on prep counter out of temperature control (not on TPHC) across for the wok station on the cookline. EHS also suggested a properly made ice bath to store TCS food items at 41F or below on the prepline during operation.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: jar of water, plastic containers of seasonings and spices (sugar, salt, msg, ground black pepper, curry powder, dried orange peels), and plastic squeeze bottles (brown sauce, oil, water) on the cookline in the main kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EHS instructed CFM to place common food name on all food items removed from original container. CHANS KITCHEN (Inspection Date: 09/16/2026) Page 2 of 3

violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. EHS instructed CFM to the shelves inside the Amerikooler walk in refrigerator.

violations.title: Handwashing Signage
violations.observation: Observed that sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided or is not clearly visible at all handwashing sinks used by food employees.
violations.corrective_action: Provide a visible sign or poster at all handwashing sinks used by food employees that reminds food employees to wash their hands. EHs provided a copy to the PIC, PIC posted handwashing signs

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: EHS observed in the walk in cooler raw marinated chicken being stored above raw shrimp, raw marinated beef and cut and washed carrots and celery.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). PIC rearranged the walk in cooler so the raw chicken was being stored below the raw beef, below the raw shrimp and below the raw cut carrots and celery. EHS provided a copy of cross contamination poster, PIC posted poster on the outside of the walk in cooler.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.title: Openings Protected from Pest Entry
violations.observation: EHS observed a 1 inch gap in the base and 3+ inch gap in the top of the rear kitchen screen door.
violations.corrective_action: Windows or doors kept open for ventilation or other purposes shall have openings that are adequately protected against the entry of insects or rodents by 1) 16 mesh to 25.4mm (16 mesh to 1 inch) screens; 2) properly designed and installed air curtains to control flying insects; or 3) other effective means EHS spoke to PIC about effective barriers against pests and agreed to have gaps around screen door repaired and sealed.

violations.title: Unpackaged Food Preparation, No Contamination
violations.observation: EHS observed unpackaged fried crispy wontons for the hot and sour soup being stored in the rear kitchen dry storage area.
violations.corrective_action: During preparation, unpackaged food, shall be protected from environmental contamination. PIC agreed to store them in the covered containers.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: EHS observed in use utensil scoops for rice and flour being stored in ingredients so the handles cannot be reach without contaminating the food.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. PIC put on gloves and removed the utensils so the handles could be reached without contaminating the food.
